subject: Predict detection probability at a specific distance and considering covariates

messages.author: 9b368da43dd6b176
messages.subject: Predict detection probability at a specific distance and considering covariates
parts:
Hi,

Is there an easy way to obtain the prediction of the detection probability considering specific covariates values and a specific distance ?

The predict function can give me an average conditional detection probability over the whole range of distance considered (0 to W or int.range), but in my case, I want to know what this detection probability is, for example, at 40 m from the observer.


#######################################
To illustrate my question:

data(book.tee.data)
egdata <- book.tee.data$book.tee.dataframe[book.tee.data$book.tee.dataframe$observer==1,]
egdata$Covar1 <- sample(seq(1,16), nrow(egdata), replace=TRUE) # Create a fake covariate
head(egdata)

result <- ddf(dsmodel=~mcds(key="hn", formula=~1), data=egdata, method="ds", meta.data=list(width=4))
predict(result, newdata=egdata) # Because no covariates were included -> same value everywhere.

result <- ddf(dsmodel=~mcds(key="hn", formula=~Covar1), data=egdata, method="ds", meta.data=list(width=4))
predict(result, newdata=egdata) # average detection probability for each specific value of the covariate


newdat <-  egdata
newdat$distance <- runif(nrow(newdat),0.1,4)
predict(result, newdata=newdat) # (Obviously) same as previous even if distance was changed

## I need the specific detection probability corresponding to the distance defined for each line of the new dataset.


Thanks

Arnaud

messages.author: 350dad0a615d36db
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Predict detection probability at a specific distance and considering covariates
parts:
Hi Arnaud, hi listfolk,

Indeed, the predict function will only tell you about the average
detectability (averaged over the distances).

The detfct() function will do just about what you want, though the
output is a little more complex...

Picking up from where you left off, you can run

detfct(1, result$ds$aux$ddfobj)

this will give you a vector of length nrow(data), as the results are
*conditional on the observed covariates*. Supplying more than one
distance at the time gets a bit fraught as you fall victim to R's vector
recycling rules, which can get a bit tricky decipher when you have
covariates. I'd advise some caution when running such code for that reason.

Hope that helps!


cheers,
--dave
